courseTitle: Ionic - Build iOS, Android & Web Apps with Ionic & Angular

cues.en: We could use autoLogin in the app component of course, that makes sense because when the app starts
in initialize app or in ngOnInit, then we certainly want to check whether the user is logged in
but an even better place might be our auth guard because that kicks it whenever we try to visit a protected
place.
So in the auth guard here, I will now still get access to userIsAuthenticated but I want to change
what I do when we're not authenticated. Instead of immediately redirecting,
I want to check whether we're able to autoLogin and therefore, I'll not use tap here but switch map
which therefore of course needs to be imported from rxjs operators and switch map now gets the
isAuthenticated information
and if we're not authenticated here, then I actually want to try the autoLogin.
So here I will return this auth service autoLogin and this should return an observable,
so in autoLogin, I am returning this observable chain and in the end, this returns true or false,
right,
that is what we just set up but it also tries logging us in automatically. If we're not authenticated,
then I'll return a new observable with auth, with the auth creation operator imported from rxjs
and there, I will just forward the isAuthenticated information as a new observable because in that
case, I'll tap in, get the isAuthenticated information and then navigate by URL and otherwise, well
just let canLoad do its job.
So now the auth guard should take care about calling autoLogin for us or not.
Now let's give this a try,
if I now save this
and the app reloads, I stay on this page because right now, we have no data stored.
Now let me login here
and I get an error, cannot read property error of undefined, in the auth page,
we have this problem. So it looks like we got an error but not from the server but from somewhere else.
Let me console log that error response temporarily to see what went wrong here when I tried to login,
invalid time value, add data to ISO string. So in my auth service, in the place where I call store
auth data and I call to ISO string on the expiration time, there we're having a problem,
probably because the generation of the expiration time fails and
the problem here is I'm not getting the expiresIn key.
You can see that if you check the network request that gets sent, which is what I did to narrow down
this issue, here,
we're missing that expiresIn key.
The reason for that is that I forgot something when I do login,
we're sending e-mail and password and what else do we need to send?
We have a look at the docs, we should send returnSecureToken which always should be true.
Well, didn't do that,
so let's add returnSecureToken here and set this to true on the login request, on the sign-up
request, I did do it and now with this, we'll get back expiresIn on the response and therefore we'll be
able to set this expiration date.
So now as this reloads here, let's login and now this looks way better,
we're allowed to visit this page and now if I reload this page,
I actually start here because now our autoLogin works. And you can see that stored data here in the
browser if you click on application,
local storage because here on the Mac, it is stored in local storage, on a real device it won't, there
it will be stored in the native device storage
but here, you can see your auth data and that is your userId and so on.
